tested:
FortiAnalyzer - had NO entry at all (found 2026-07-18 device audit: device_id
1f5a2e4a-3e7a-488c-ad36-03c0ab04f30d, image "fortinet-FAZ-6-4"). Every other
lookup path (image-manager detector.py taxonomy, image_profiles.py disk-bus table)
already recognises "fortianalyzer"/"faz", but this file - the authoritative table
node-manager's QemuProvider actually reads for RAM/vCPU - had nothing, so
get_profile() silently fell through to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE (512MB/1 vCPU). Live
repro (2026-07-18, isolated single-node lab, host otherwise idle): the domain
reached libvirt RUNNING quickly (process launched fine - NOT a disk-bus/machine-type
problem, virtio already matches the virtioa.qcow2 filename) but then sat pinned at
~99% CPU / ~484MB of its 512MB cap (94%) indefinitely with zero settling over 100+s
of polling - the classic signature of a guest that can never finish booting inside
its memory ceiling. Fortinet's own KVM admin guide (docs.fortinet.com, all versions
6.4-8.0) states FortiAnalyzer-VM's minimum is 4 vCPU / 8GB RAM (16GB for 7.4.1+);
this image is the 6.4 build, so 8GB is the correct floor. Matches the
fortinet-fortigate entry above precedent: set default = the real vendor minimum,
not the generic fallback.

reasons.emulator:
cpu_model "qemu64", not "host" (NPX-1527 PROFILES-TOOLS pass-3, rule #59):
EVE-NG's real fortinet.yml (the one template all 4 FortiOS-family keys in this
file map to) sets NO -cpu flag at all, which QEMU defaults to qemu64 - "host" here
was undocumented drift with no cited crash/boot evidence (unlike the RAM values on
these same entries, which do carry real cited evidence). Matching EVE's real,
verified-safe default until/unless a live boot specifically justifies "host".
NOT live-boot-verified either way this pass - if a future boot needs "host",
cite the evidence here per rule #59 before changing it back.
reasons.config_dialect:
Wave 21 (2026-09-10): FortiAnalyzer is NOT FortiOS's CLI, despite sharing a
vendor string with FortiGate - live-measured on a real boot (rule #22/#30):
`show full-configuration` (the "fortinet"/FortiOS dialect's capture command)
gets "command parse error before 'full-configuration'"; plain `show` at the
same prompt returns the full config. See VENDOR_CLI["fortianalyzer"].

settings.description: Fortinet FortiAnalyzer VM - vendor minimum is 4 vCPU / 8GB RAM (docs.fortinet.com KVM admin guide); the generic 512MB fallback never finishes booting (guest pins at ~99% CPU / ~94% RAM forever).
